source.title: Interpreting ResNet-based CLIP via Neuron-Attention Decomposition

record.tranche_reason: The study compares neuron-only representations with neuron-head pairs and reports that neuron-only representations are less well captured by a single direction and less sparse. This refines the claim that neurons are consistently interpretable units, but it does not estimate an interpretable-neuron share.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for CLIP-ResNet components, including neuron-only and neuron-head decompositions. Segmentation and distribution-shift results are not recorded because they evaluate downstream applications rather than the claim versions. It does not test language-model neuron poles, InceptionV1 examples, attribution graphs, or explanation scoring on held-out activations.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a neuron-head decomposition for CLIP-ResNet's final layer. It shows neuron-head pairs are more rank-1, sparser and less clustered than whole neurons. Its measures (reconstruction accuracy, mean-ablation sparsity, top-image inertia) are proxies for its method's properties, not a share of interpretable neurons. It has no language-model neuron audit (V1/V2), no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron (V3) and no attribution graphs (V5). It does not score explanations against held-out activations (V6/V7). Neuron-head pairs are a different unit from neurons, so the better-tool result does not measure V4's interpretable-neuron share. The original source Bills et al. is cited only as related work. The reader's V3 link is wrong: no canonical polysemantic example is re-examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that neuron-head pairs in CLIP-ResNet are approximately rank-1 and sparse, unlike neurons, and can be labelled with text. Some pairs capture sub-concepts of their neuron, while pairs can still be polysemantic. They present the pairs as relatively interpretable units useful for segmentation and shift monitoring.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies image-encoder neuron and attention-head contributions in CLIP-ResNet, not language-model neuron poles or tested natural-language explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The representation unit changes the results: neuron-head pairs are more rank-1 and sparse than neuron-only contributions. RN50x64 neuron representations reconstruct with higher fidelity than RN50x16 neuron representations at the same number of principal components.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP-ResNet's last layer, whole-neuron output contributions are not rank-1. Their top-image clusters have higher inertia than neuron-head pairs, while some neuron-head pairs remain polysemantic. A finer path-level decomposition yields more coherent units than neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In CLIP-ResNet, decomposing last-layer neurons by attention-pooling head yields units that are lower-rank, sparser and less polysemantic (by image-cluster inertia) than whole neurons.

record.problems: The interpretability comparison relies on reconstruction accuracy, sparsity, and image-cluster inertia as proxies; it does not measure a percentage of individually interpretable neurons. Some reported comparisons are qualitative or lack exact values in the text. The study uses 1000 images for its contribution dataset D and reports that neuron-head pairs remain polysemantic.
record.rows_left_out: Left out downstream semantic-segmentation and dataset-shift results because they concern applications rather than the claim versions. Also left out attention-head-only comparisons and detailed example labels because they do not directly measure neuron interpretability.
record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V4 and declared V3. Neither fits: V3 concerns re-reading InceptionV1-style polysemantic neurons, and V4 concerns interpretable-neuron share rising with tools and architecture. Neuron-head pairs are not neurons. Segmentation and shift results are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Only the relative properties of neuron-only and neuron-head representations in CLIP-ResNet are examined. No share of interpretable neurons is estimated, and no causal attribution of interpretability to architecture, regularization, or tool quality is tested.

relation.reason: Neuron polysemanticity is only motivation here, and Bills et al. 2023 is cited in passing. The reader's tests/T5 call is not supported.

tranche.reason: This is a vision paper that decomposes CLIP-ResNet. It measures rank-1 structure, sparsity and inertia for its own neuron-head unit. It gives no share of interpretable neurons and no test of any version.

source_check.notes: All 8 rows match the text, including where the Table 1 and Table 5 cells sit. Figure 1-3 values are plot-only. r6's op reads as ablating the top 10%; the text keeps the top 10% and mean-ablates the rest, and the condition field has this right. r8's raw-count comparison is confounded by unit counts: about 147,000 pairs versus a few thousand neurons in RN50x16.
